text:
nitya: quick heads-up 99found a couple of broken anchors on Troubleshooting -> Rate limits and the current CLI repro for 429s uses a legacy header `X-Old-Rate`, so the curl snippet fails for new users. i'll open a small PR to patch anchors and replace the snippet with a curl that captures headers + tiny backoff examples.

olivia: which anchors specifically? paste the problematic URL and anchor so i can verify redirect behavior.

nitya: page: https://docs.redwood.ai/troubleshooting/rate-limits anchor `#repro-locally` returns 404 because our docs host redirects `/troubleshooting/...` -> `/guides/...` and strips anchors. also curl missed `-D -` so users can't see `Retry-After` and it referenced `X-Old-Rate` in headers.

conor: we should fix routing long-term but a docs PR is the quick fix. include a short "how to repro safely" that shows capturing headers and suggests parsing `Retry-After`. link to ops netem (internal) for traffic shaping. keep netem out of the main snippet.

nitya: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/6027 - changes: fix anchors, add curl + minimal node/python backoff snippets, add note about `-D -`, and link to ops netem quick-start. requesting review from @olivia and @sam.

sam: i'll take review. quick asks: keep examples minimal (one-liner curl + 3-line py/node examples). do not include deep netem steps inline.

nitya: updated PR to keep netem as a link: https://go.redwood/ops/netem-quick. added a concise repro command: 

    # reproduce token-window 429 locally (simulate burst)
    TOKEN=...; curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -X POST "https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate" -d '{"prompt":"x","max_tokens":10}' -D - --max-time 8

olivia: nice. tiny nit 99explain `-D -` briefly so readers know it dumps response headers. also confirm the API host is `api.redwood.com` in the snippet (looks good).

nitya: added a one-line explanation for `-D -` and a small python backoff example.

sam: saw the python snippet, left one nit about phrasing around `Retry-After` parsing. can you add a 3-line pseudo-code for exponential backoff with jitter and show precedence: if `Retry-After` present use it, else use exponential backoff? keep it concise.

nitya: added this python pseudo-snippet in the PR (kept to 3 lines): 

    import time, random
    def backoff(attempt, base=0.5, cap=10):
        sleep = min(cap, base * 2**attempt); time.sleep(sleep + random.uniform(0, sleep*0.1))
    # if resp.status_code == 429: if 'Retry-After' in resp.headers: time.sleep(int(resp.headers['Retry-After'])) else: backoff(attempt)

conor: small suggestion: add a single-sentence :warning: that any client-side backoff should respect upstream route SLAs and not mask real latency problems. otherwise LGTM.

olivia: LGTM with that warning added. Sam, can you approve so we can merge to staging?

sam: /approve. CI green on my side; merging after the final run.

nitya: merging once CI finishes, will ping #release for a staging deploy. also creating a follow-up issue to scan other troubleshooting pages for anchor rot: tracking issue #6028. thanks all for the quick reviews. :shipit:

docs-bot: label added: needs-staging-sync

nitya: CI passed; merged and pushed to staging. pinging #release for a quick staging deploy.
